sections.h2: The August Act removed both notifications the Budget's exemption required

chart.title: Both notifications the Budget required fell away, from 2 to 0
chart.sub: Government notifications needed for the exemption, by version of the law.
chart.source: Finance Act 2026; Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act 2026.

sections.means: The exemption became an entitlement, so any foreign company meeting the conditions and filing the prescribed information now qualifies.
sections.todo: Notify the data centre rules, which the Act leaves to rules that had not been notified.

sections.h2: India still taxes the Indian operator: about Rs 3.78 on a Rs 115 payment

chart.title: Of Rs 115 paid, Rs 3.78 is Indian tax and Rs 11.22 is profit after tax
chart.sub: Split of Rs 115 paid to an Indian related operator under the 15% cost-plus safe harbour, in rupees.
chart.source: Safe harbour as described in this post; blog arithmetic at the 25.17% corporate rate.

sections.means: The Indian operator's tax is small, about 3.3% of what the foreign company pays it, while the foreign company's resale income abroad is exempt.
sections.todo: Publish an official estimate of the revenue forgone, since none was found and none could be made without knowing the booked volume.

sections.h2: Parliament passed the Act six days after its introduction, on 10 August

chart.title: The Budget promise became law in six months, with Parliament passing it on 10 August

sections.means: The Bill passed both Houses within six days of introduction and received assent on 17 August, replacing the June ordinance.
